topic: Who will really use AI heavily at work
angle: Enterprise AI usage will be uneven—optimize for power users, not average users.
sourceTitle: Will anybody use AI as much as coders do?
linkedinPost:
Most employees won’t use AI like coders do—and that’s OK if you plan for it.

The Economist asks whether any job will see AI usage as intense as software development. From what I’ve seen in large deployments, usage concentrates: a minority become power users, a big middle dabbles, and a chunk opts out.

My take: design your AI program for the distribution you actually get, not the average you wish for. Invest in enablement for the top 10–20% who’ll move the needle (playbooks, prompts, workflow integration), and stop overpaying for idle seats. License based on verified active use, not ambition.

Pick use cases with high task frequency and tight feedback loops—claims triage, QA checks, sales email drafting—where power users can compound gains daily. Then let their playbooks pull the middle forward.

If adoption lags, it’s usually because the workflow didn’t change. Tools don’t transform outcomes; redesigned processes do.

How are you measuring real adoption (not just logins) and reallocating budget toward your power users? #AIStrategy #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI
